deviation.upstream: Upstream discards every deletion result and disconnect carries on as a success: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:21-23 - :22 APIKeychain.delete(account(server: server, field: field)); DroppyCode/Services/Providers/APIKeychain.swift:76-83 - :82 SecItemDelete(query as CFDictionary); DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:118-120 - :118 MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server: entry) | :119 if entry.isOAuth { | :120 MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID: entry.id); DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPOAuth.swift:189-191 - :190 MCPKeychain.delete(server: serverID, field: "oauth") | :191 MCPKeychain.delete(server: serverID, field: "oauth-client"); upstream reports nothing, so it has no wording for the report
deviation.port: Marrow checks each credential deletion that disconnect makes and reports a failed one to the user instead of success (BLK-0012 ruling: "a failed credential deletion on disconnect is reported to the user instead of success"). Three details are ENGINEERING DECISIONS, not ruling text: the two OAuth items signOut deletes during disconnect (MCPStore.swift:119-120) are included, because they are credential deletions made on disconnect, although BLK-0012's quarantined sub-path names only deleteAll; an item that did not exist is not a failure, because upstream routinely deletes items that were never written (deleteAll walks every declared field whether set or not, and signOut deletes both OAuth items whether present or not); and the rest of disconnect still runs, because upstream's disconnect has no early exit (MCPStore.swift:115-128) and the ruling changes only what is reported. The report reads, per OD-0012 E6: "Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values." Where it is shown is not given by the source or by the ruling (open_question).

records.open_question: OD-0012 E6 gives the text of the failed-deletion report ("Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values.") but neither the ruling nor the source says where it is shown or for how long.

deviation.upstream: Upstream discards every deletion result and disconnect carries on as a success: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:21-23 - :22 APIKeychain.delete(account(server: server, field: field)); DroppyCode/Services/Providers/APIKeychain.swift:76-83 - :82 SecItemDelete(query as CFDictionary); DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:118-120 - :118 MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server: entry) | :119 if entry.isOAuth { | :120 MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID: entry.id); DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPOAuth.swift:189-191 - :190 MCPKeychain.delete(server: serverID, field: "oauth") | :191 MCPKeychain.delete(server: serverID, field: "oauth-client"); upstream reports nothing, so it has no wording for the report
deviation.port: Marrow checks each credential deletion that disconnect makes and reports a failed one to the user instead of success (BLK-0012 ruling: "a failed credential deletion on disconnect is reported to the user instead of success"). Three details are ENGINEERING DECISIONS, not ruling text: the two OAuth items signOut deletes during disconnect (MCPStore.swift:119-120) are included, because they are credential deletions made on disconnect, although BLK-0012's quarantined sub-path names only deleteAll; an item that did not exist is not a failure, because upstream routinely deletes items that were never written (deleteAll walks every declared field whether set or not, and signOut deletes both OAuth items whether present or not); and the rest of disconnect still runs, because upstream's disconnect has no early exit (MCPStore.swift:115-128) and the ruling changes only what is reported. The report reads, per OD-0012 E6: "Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values." Where it is shown is not given by the source or by the ruling (open_question).

records.open_question: OD-0012 E6 gives the text of the failed-deletion report ("Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values.") but neither the ruling nor the source says where it is shown or for how long.

records.geometry: The page is a VStack with alignment leading and spacing Chrome.sectionSpacing = 20 holding one ProviderSettingsSection per ProviderKind: every signed-in provider first, then every other provider, each group in allCases order. Each section is a VStack with alignment leading and spacing Chrome.sectionHeaderSpacing = 10 holding the header toggle (UI-PROVREG-045) and then a ChromeRevealLayout wrapping a ChromeCard. The header is 22 points high. The reveal slot is the card's natural height times the fraction (1 expanded, 0 collapsed), and the card is placed top-leading at full size so it never moves; the clip reveals it in place. The card is an eager VStack with spacing 0 (ChromeCard's lazy flag defaults to false and this page passes none) on a RoundedRectangle of corner radius Chrome.cardCornerRadius = 16, continuous style, filled with Chrome.overlay(0.03). Read from the code, not executed: the reveal slot is the second child of the spacing-10 VStack, so by standard SwiftUI VStack spacing a collapsed section keeps the 10 point gap under its 22 point header and is 32 points tall.

records.colors: Card fill is Chrome.primaryText at opacity 0.03, which resolves per appearance because it wraps the AppKit labelColor.

records.notes: The sections are built EAGERLY, not lazily, and so is each card's own row stack (ChromeCard without lazy: true). The source comment records why: lazy sections were rebuilt while scrolling, which reset their text fields and re-ran every check they started on appear. A port that uses a virtualised list here will reintroduce that bug. Collapsing does not unmount a section either, so its fields keep their values and its onAppear and onChange handlers still run while it is collapsed. The per-provider expansion overrides live in the page's state for the page's lifetime and are never persisted. All 14 sections are always present, so there is no empty state for the page itself.

states: 0 percent: no fill drawn at all
any value above 0 but very small: a 5 point minimum stub, so a nearly empty bar is still visible
75 and above: warning hue
90 and above: danger hue
interactions: none; it is not interactive
records.notes: The view takes a FRACTION, and the caller divides the percent by 100, so the two scales must not be confused. The thresholds are compared against the PERCENT, not the fraction. Accessibility: the element is labelled with the window title and its value is the clamped percentage followed by the literal "% used", because a bare percentage said nothing about which window it belonged to.

Row spacing between any two timeline rows is TimelineMetrics.rowSpacing = 20; a message reserves TimelineMetrics.hoverLineHeight = 22 inside the row for its hover controls.

records.notes: The row is created only when the first delta carries text, so a provider that opens a text block with an empty delta leaves no blank reply row. The row id is the provider's own id, which is how later completions and delegation scans address it.

records.element: The /plan command, typed or picked from the suggestions
records.geometry: This area defines the outgoing text, not the chip. ComposerDraft.outgoingText builds the head as "/" followed by the command name; with an empty body the head alone goes out, with quotes present the head is joined to the body by two newlines, and otherwise by a single space (ThreadRuntime.swift:122-135). The chip that stands for a DraftCommand is drawn by the composer view, outside this area.
records.typography: Set by the composer, outside this area.
records.colors: Set by the composer, outside this area.
states: Recognised only when the whole trimmed outgoing text is exactly "/plan"; "/plan something" is sent to the provider instead. Recognised on every send path: the composer send, the follow-up queue drain, send-now and the Return-captured pending send.
interactions: Sending it toggles ChatThread.interactionMode between .plan and .build and records "plan" in the provider recency list. No turn starts and no message reaches the provider.
records.notes: It looks like a provider slash command but never leaves the app. A port that forwarded it would put the thread in plan mode AND send a stray command to the provider.

records.element: Terminal drawer panel (the whole sheet rising from the bottom of the chat column)
records.geometry: Full pane width. Height = dragHeight ?? settings.terminalHeight (default 260, applied unclamped; drag clamps 140...760). Background UnevenRoundedRectangle with topLeadingRadius 16, topTrailingRadius 16, style .continuous, square bottom corners. Internal layout VStack(spacing: 0): a 38-point tab row then the terminal or the empty state.
records.typography: n/a
records.colors: Fill Color(white: 0.08) in dark, Color(white: 0.985) in light. Literal greys, not theme tokens; identical to the terminal view's own background so there is no seam.
states: visible: mounted with a move-from-bottom plus opacity transition under Chrome.panelSlide
hidden: unmounted; shells keep running
resizing: height follows the pointer and the chat pane is flagged as live-resizing
thread switching: the visibility animation is nil, so the change is instant
empty: the tab strip is empty and the body shows the empty state
interactions: drag the 8-point top strip to resize
Escape while the composer has focus hides it (after a running turn, before the changes panel)
Escape inside the terminal at the shell prompt hides it
upstream: Command-J, the chrome Terminal button, the View menu item and the palette action all toggle it
port: the chord (Ctrl+J by default, OD-0008 B7), the chrome Terminal button and the palette action toggle it; there is no View menu item because there is no menu bar (OD-0008 C3)
records.notes: The persisted height is applied with NO clamp (upstream defect 70). Do not add a load-time clamp; the 140...760 bounds exist only inside the drag handler.

records.typography: TerminalFont.preferred() (TerminalFont.swift:8-16), read once when the session is created: the first configured terminal font (Ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal.app; running ones first) that covers the four Nerd probe glyphs; else, with a configured font, its Nerd sibling family at its size, else the first installed Nerd Font at its size, else that configured font; with no configured font, the first installed Nerd Font at 12 points, else NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular).
records.colors: Dark: background white 0.08, foreground white 0.9. Light: background white 0.985, foreground white 0.12. Caret = Chrome.accentNSColor (theme accent, or the system control accent for System, Light and Dark). Selection background = that accent at 0.3 alpha. The 16 ANSI colours are SwiftTerm 1.20.0 defaults and are not configured anywhere in the source.
states: focused: takes the keyboard once when the drawer is opened

focused: the caret is a block that fades out in about 0.64 s and back in about 0.64 s, a cycle of about 1.4 s (MacCaretView.swift:104-123; catalogue terminal.block-cursor-blink, 2-chat-use.mov S 132.237-134.31); unfocused: an outline that does not blink
exited: keeps showing its final scrollback; the tab dims
window live-resizing: autoresizing parked, frame synced at most every 50 ms, one final sync on release
interactions: all keyboard input goes to the shell
Option is sent as Meta (optionAsMetaKey = true)

mouse selection uses SwiftTerm's own handling (SwiftTerm 1.20.0 MacTerminalView.swift:2878-3012 with SelectionService.swift): a double click selects the word (letters, digits and . _ -) or the balanced bracket expression under the pointer, a triple click the line, a shift click extends the selection, a press-drag selects; after a double click a drag keeps the seed word and snaps to words, after a triple click it grows by lines

a program that asked for the mouse (DECSET 9, 1000, 1002, 1003; encodings 1005, 1006, 1015, 1016; XTSHIFTESCAPE CSI > Ps s) is told of presses, releases, drags, motion and the wheel (Terminal.swift:6916-6999, MacTerminalView.swift:2878-3270); shift selects locally unless the program asked for shift clicks
the pointer is the I-beam over the body (MacTerminalView.swift:3271-3273; catalogue pointer.ibeam-text)
records.notes: There is no Droppy setting anywhere for terminal font, size, cursor style or palette; the face and size can come from another terminal application's configuration (PR-TERM-124 to PR-TERM-134). The view is a single long-lived object reparented between containers, never rebuilt, so scrollback survives tab and thread switches, and its font is not re-read after creation. OD-0013 (owner ruling): the main window chrome is not accepted until the one-frame live-resize edge strip probe P4 measured is gone (3-5 px of the window's own backdrop without the app layer at the growing edges, clipping for about a frame at the shrinking edges); it is not downgraded to a deviation.
